Dear Cody,

as far as I know, Andy's R code was the basis for quite a bit of the original developments in unmarked, including occuRN. Hence, I would expect exactly the same results. On the other hand, quite possible that some smaller things changed, perhaps the way in which missing values were dealt with or something.

I would say, take unmarked and don't worry about the older code.

Best regards --- Marc

messages.author: 1195ce743af3d0d7
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] comparing occuRN and panel 4.3 from Royle and Dorazio (2008)
parts:
Hey Mark,

Thanks for the input, I am using the code from the 2008 book because I need to be able to use it with the Integrated SDM framework developed by Dorazio (2014) and Koshkina et al (2017). I'm not sure how I would do this using unmarked, but it is doable using custom code (i.e. borrowing from the 2008 book). 

I think you are right, it has to do with how missing data is handled. Are there any guidelines for how much missing data is too much? Depending on how many sampling occasions I use, I have up to 40% missing data. 

Thanks
Cody
